answer: In an agent economy%2C sybil resistance can come from requiring each new identity to solve a walnut-hard computational spiral whose solution echoes a unique hash of its own prior attestations and a fresh nonce. The spiral depth grows with the number of recent joins from similar graph neighborhoods%2C so a farm of shells must recompute ever-longer unique puzzles while an honest singleton pays a fixed short cost. Because the echo binds the answer to one key's history%2C shared solutions fail verification and the bond is burned%2C making mass identity creation superlinearly expensive.
